turn_0002.0: 🧠 The human brain – Lesson 1: The amazing world of the brain
turn_0002.1: The brain is one of the most complex and remarkable organs in the human body.
turn_0002.2: The brain plays an important role in everything we do: thinking, speaking, remembering, dreaming, loving, feeling fear, and making decisions.
turn_0002.3: Let's learn about it from the basics, with simple explanations, scientific details, and examples.
turn_0002.4: 1. What is the human brain like?
turn_0002.54: Some important facts about the brain:
turn_0002.55: The average adult human brain weighs about 1.3–1.4 kilograms.
turn_0002.59: The brain contains about 86 billion neurons.
turn_0002.63: The brain uses a considerable amount of energy even when the body is at rest.
turn_0002.67: The brain is protected by the skull.
turn_0002.71: The brain continues to function even while we sleep.
turn_0002.76: 2. The three main parts of the brain
turn_0002.92: It plays a major role in thinking, memory, language, understanding sensations, planning, and voluntary movements.
turn_0002.111: It helps with balance, coordination of muscle movements, and precision of movement.
turn_0002.131: It regulates functions essential for survival, such as breathing, heartbeat, and alertness.
turn_0002.136: The brain contains specialized nerve cells called neurons. They exchange information through electrical and chemical signals.
turn_0002.152: For example, if you touch a hot pan:
turn_0002.163: The spinal cord triggers an immediate withdrawal reflex
turn_0002.167: The hand pulls away quickly; the brain senses the pain
turn_0002.170: This is called a reflex action. Not every movement needs a prior command from the brain.
turn_0002.172: Suppose you learn a new word today.
turn_0002.173: The brain processes that information. As you use it repeatedly, connections between neurons change, helping you recall it later.
turn_0002.174: This ability to change is called neuroplasticity.
turn_0002.175: That is why practice helps us learn skills such as a new language, music, or mathematics.

turn_0003.0: Do all the lobes work at the same time?

turn_0004.0: Yes! 🧠 All the lobes of the human brain can work at the same time. But they do not all work at the same level of activity. Depending on what we are doing, some areas become more active while others are relatively less active.
turn_0004.1: 1. The four main lobes of the brain
turn_0004.24: Touch, body sensations, and spatial awareness
turn_0004.34: 2. How do they work at the same time?
turn_0004.35: For example, suppose you are walking down a street while talking with a friend.
turn_0004.51: It helps you decide what to say, how to respond, and how to walk.
turn_0004.70: It helps you understand the position of your legs, body sensations, and the space around you.
turn_0004.89: It helps you understand your friend's speech and the meaning of the words.
turn_0004.108: It processes visual information from the road, vehicles, people, and other things.
turn_0004.112: Because the four lobes work together in this way, you can walk, see, hear, and speak.
turn_0004.113: 3. Does one lobe work on its own?
turn_0004.115: For example, when you look at an apple:
turn_0004.116: Occipital lobe — processes visual information such as the apple's color and shape.
turn_0004.120: Temporal lobe — helps identify what the object is.
turn_0004.124: Parietal lobe — helps determine where it is.
turn_0004.128: Frontal lobe — helps decide whether to pick it up.
turn_0004.133: Rather than acting like separate machines, these areas work as interconnected neural networks.
turn_0004.135: Working at the same time does not mean that all neurons fire at the same time.
turn_0004.136: Different groups of neurons in different brain regions become active as needed. Many networks in the brain remain active even at rest.
turn_0004.138: Now, an interesting question for you:

turn_0006.0: Yes! 🧠 The human brain is the body's main control center. But the brain does not work alone. It controls the body together with the spinal cord and nerves.
turn_0006.1: 1. How does the brain control the body?
turn_0006.16: For example, suppose you want to raise your right hand.
turn_0006.20: Creates a motor signal to raise the hand
turn_0006.30: Send the signal to the muscles
turn_0006.36: The muscles contract and the hand rises!
turn_0006.40: The motor cortex in the frontal lobe mainly helps control voluntary body movements.
turn_0006.57: The motor cortex on the left side of the brain mainly controls movements on the right side of the body.
turn_0006.61: The motor cortex on the right side of the brain mainly controls movements on the left side of the body.
turn_0006.66: 3. What actions happen without us thinking about them?
turn_0006.67: Many functions, such as heartbeat, breathing, and digestion, occur without our conscious control.
turn_0006.68: The brainstem, autonomic nervous system, and other body systems take part in these functions. The spinal cord can immediately coordinate some reflex actions.
turn_0006.69: Key point to remember: The brain controls the body and also constantly receives information from it. This is two-way communication.
